acceptance_criteria: The app can be installed from a clean checkout with one package-manager command
The app can run locally in development mode
The app has a minimal landing/game shell route
The project includes lint, test, and build scripts
The README documents setup and local run commands
tasks.description: Create the initial web app project for a browser-based 3D chess game. Use a modern frontend stack suitable for 3D rendering, typed code, and testability. Include a clean project structure, package scripts, linting, formatting, and a minimal home screen.
tasks.title: Create the 3D chess web app scaffold

acceptance_criteria: Board state can be initialized to the standard chess starting position
Legal moves are generated for all piece types
Illegal moves are rejected
Check, checkmate, and stalemate are detected
Castling, en passant, and promotion are supported
Move history can be replayed or inspected
The chess engine has unit tests for normal and edge-case rules
tasks.description: Implement the core chess domain model independent of UI rendering. Represent board state, pieces, turns, legal moves, captures, check, checkmate, stalemate, castling, en passant, promotion, and game history.
tasks.title: Define chess domain model and legal move engine

acceptance_criteria: A 3D chessboard renders in the browser
All chess pieces render in their correct starting positions
The scene uses lighting and shadows
The board is responsive to browser size
The camera has a pleasing default angle
The implementation exposes helpers for converting board squares to scene positions
tasks.description: Render a polished 3D chess board and pieces in the browser. Use realistic lighting, shadows, camera controls, smooth layout, and responsive sizing. The scene should support mapping chess squares to 3D coordinates.
tasks.title: Build the 3D board and piece rendering foundation

acceptance_criteria: The 3D board is rendered from chess engine state
Making a legal move updates the board
Captured pieces are removed from the board
Promotion changes the piece type
The UI displays whose turn it is
The UI displays check, checkmate, and stalemate states
tasks.description: Connect the chess domain model to the 3D board. Pieces should render from game state, moves should update state, captured pieces should disappear, promotions should update piece identity, and the current player should be visible.
tasks.title: Connect chess engine state to the 3D scene

acceptance_criteria: Users can select pieces by clicking or tapping
Legal destinations are highlighted
Capture moves are visually distinct
Illegal moves are blocked and produce subtle feedback
Pieces animate smoothly from source square to destination square
Mouse and touch interactions both work
tasks.description: Allow users to select and move pieces using mouse or touch. Highlight selected pieces, legal destinations, captures, and invalid moves. Include smooth piece movement animations.
tasks.title: Implement mouse and touch interaction for moving pieces

acceptance_criteria: The AI can select a legal move from any valid non-terminal board state
Easy mode makes quick beginner-level moves
Medium mode uses board evaluation and shallow search
Hard mode uses deeper search with alpha-beta pruning
The AI never returns illegal moves
AI move selection does not freeze the UI for normal positions
AI behavior has unit tests for legality and deterministic seeded cases
tasks.description: Implement local AI for human-versus-AI play. Easy should make simple or partially random legal moves. Medium should use a basic evaluation function and shallow search. Hard should use deeper search, alpha-beta pruning, and a stronger evaluation function while staying responsive in the browser.
tasks.title: Create AI move engine with Easy, Medium, and Hard modes

acceptance_criteria: The user can choose Human vs AI mode
The user can select Easy, Medium, or Hard difficulty
The AI makes a move after the human move completes
The UI indicates when the AI is thinking
The user cannot move while the AI is thinking
The game correctly handles human win, AI win, stalemate, and draw states
tasks.description: Add a game mode where the human plays against the AI. Include difficulty selection for Easy, Medium, and Hard. The AI should automatically move after the human completes a valid move.
tasks.title: Add human-versus-AI game mode

acceptance_criteria: The user can request a hint during their turn
The hint shows the recommended source and destination squares
The hint move is always legal
The hint updates when the board state changes
The hint can be dismissed or replaced by the next move
Hint mode does not make the move automatically
tasks.description: Add a hint feature that computes and displays the next recommended move for the current player. The hint should be visually clear but not disruptive. It should use the AI evaluation system and respect the current game state.
tasks.title: Add hint mode showing the next best move

acceptance_criteria: The user can restart a game
The user can resign a game
The user can view move history in algebraic or readable notation
Captured pieces are displayed
Undo works in local play and handles AI turns consistently
Controls are disabled when unavailable
tasks.description: Add complete game controls and supporting UI. Users should be able to restart the game, undo moves where allowed, resign, view move history, and see captured pieces.
tasks.title: Add game controls, move history, undo, restart, and resign

acceptance_criteria: The app has a polished visual identity
The 3D board and surrounding UI feel cohesive
Animations are smooth and not distracting
Game state transitions are visually clear
The app looks good on desktop and tablet-sized screens
The app has a visually appealing game-over state
The app includes subtle sound or visual feedback if appropriate and configurable
tasks.description: Polish the app into a beautiful production-feeling experience. Add premium visual styling, elegant typography, responsive layout, animations, empty states, loading states, game-over presentation, and a cohesive visual theme.
tasks.title: Create beautiful visual design and fit-and-finish pass

acceptance_criteria: Interactive controls have accessible labels
Keyboard users can navigate game controls
Board selection has a keyboard-accessible path or fallback representation
Move highlights are not communicated by color alone
Reduced-motion preferences are respected
The app has no obvious accessibility violations in automated checks
tasks.description: Make the game usable with keyboard navigation and assistive technologies where practical for a 3D game. Provide accessible labels, focus states, reduced motion support, and non-color-only move indicators.
tasks.title: Add accessibility and keyboard support

acceptance_criteria: The current game is saved locally
Reloading the app restores the current game
The user can clear saved game state
Persistence handles schema version changes gracefully
Corrupt saved state does not crash the app
tasks.description: Persist the current game locally so the user can close and reopen the browser without losing progress. Include safe reset behavior and versioned persistence format.
tasks.title: Add save/load and local game persistence

acceptance_criteria: An end-to-end test confirms the app loads
An end-to-end test confirms a legal human move can be made
An end-to-end test confirms AI response behavior
An end-to-end test confirms hint mode displays a recommendation
An end-to-end test confirms restart behavior
The end-to-end tests run from a documented package script
tasks.description: Add browser-level smoke tests that verify the app loads, a human can move a piece, the AI can respond, hint mode displays a legal recommendation, and restart works.
tasks.title: Add end-to-end smoke tests for core gameplay

acceptance_criteria: The app remains responsive during AI thinking
Hard mode avoids unacceptable UI freezing
3D rendering is smooth on typical laptop hardware
Assets are loaded efficiently
Unnecessary re-renders are reduced
Performance-sensitive code has comments or documentation explaining tradeoffs
tasks.description: Profile and optimize rendering, asset loading, AI move calculation, and state updates. The app should feel smooth during interaction and avoid long main-thread stalls.
tasks.title: Optimize performance for 3D rendering and AI responsiveness

acceptance_criteria: A new developer can install, run, test, and build the app from the README
Human versus AI works on Easy, Medium, and Hard
Hint mode shows a legal recommended move
The chess rules engine correctly handles major rules and terminal states
The UI is polished and responsive
All validation commands pass
Known limitations are documented
tasks.description: Perform a final acceptance pass across functionality, visual polish, tests, documentation, and local developer experience. Fix any defects found during acceptance.
tasks.title: Create final product acceptance pass
